rules.rule: Check for traumatised/abused patient urgent signs and abuse type
rules.problem: It checks for Intimidation (the patient's own aggressive behaviour) instead of the patient being intimidated. Harassment, being ridiculed/controlled, insulted and unusual wounds from the Abuse row are not checked for. The trigger itself is reasonable.

The page gives four 'suspect abuse' criteria: discloses, examination contradicts history, abuse clear on examination, behaviour seems strange. Only the last (Abnormal behavior) is encoded. Also, the page's 'consider other types of abuse' (unwelcome behaviour, manipulation or violation) has no possible diagnosis rule.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable sexual assault/rape (traumatised/abused patient page)
Diagnose probable physical abuse (traumatised/abused patient page)
rules.problem: A bare Scar matches any scar, and the Victim of psychological trauma gate lets a patient traumatised by something other than abuse, who has a surgical scar, reach 'physical abuse probable'. 'Unusual wounds' is missing from the or-branch.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable emotional/verbal/psychological abuse (traumatised/abused patient page)
rules.problem: The Intimidation concept has the wrong direction (aggressor, not victim). Harassment, ridiculed/controlled and insulted are omitted. Only emotional abuse is diagnosed, not verbal or psychological, and the psychological-trauma gate lets anxiety after an accident yield emotional abuse.

rules.rule: Urgent: traumatised/abused patient with recent sexual assault, injuries or suicide risk
rules.problem: Its structure and Urgent level match the red box. But the 5-day and 3-day windows are measured from onset, which is when the finding is recorded, not when the assault happened, so the time limit doesn't really work. 'Injuries needing attention' has lost its qualifier, so any injury makes the patient Urgent.

summary: The most consequential problem is the Intimidation concept, used in both the check_for and the emotional abuse rule. In SNOMED it is a child of Aggressive behavior, so it records the patient as the aggressor, the opposite of the page. The red box's 5-day (woman) and 3-day (man) windows depend on onset, which is when the finding is recorded, so they hardly discriminate, and 'injuries needing attention' has lost its qualifier. The 'suspect abuse' rule encodes only one of four criteria, 'consider other types of abuse' is missing, and a bare Scar plus the psychological-trauma gate make 'physical abuse probable' too easy to reach.
